Analyze specific compliance requirements and obligations under GDPR (EU), CCPA/CPRA (California/US), and Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL, China) specifically tailored to an AI Agent application. The AI Agent collects precise location data, chat logs/records, and telemetry/usage behavior. Research must cover:
1. Legal bases and consent mechanisms for each jurisdiction: Explicit consent for sensitive personal information (precise location in China PIPL and GDPR/CCPA, sensitive data rules), separate consent obligations under PIPL, opt-in vs opt-out requirements.
2. Data minimization, storage limitation, and retention policies for AI chat histories and prompt inputs/outputs.
3. User Rights Management (Data Subject Access Requests / DSARs): right to access, delete, correct, portability, opt-out of processing/sale/sharing, and handling un-learning / data deletion requests in AI training datasets or memory vectors.
4. Privacy Notice & Transparency requirements: Disclosing AI interaction, training on user data, automated processing, clear dual-language (Chinese/English/EU languages) privacy notices.
5. Automated Decision-Making (ADM) & Profiling rules: GDPR Article 22 human-in-the-loop requirements, PIPL Article 24 transparency and opt-out rules, CCPA/CPRA rules on automated decision-making technology. Focus on official texts and regulatory guidance (CAC, EDPB, CPPA).

China CBDT mechanisms under CAC regulations, including the Provisions on Promoting and Standardizing Cross-Border Data Flows (promulgated in March 2024): Thresholds for Security Assessment, CAC Standard Contract filing, and Certification. Exemptions for personal information transfers (e.g. contract performance, non-sensitive thresholds).
2. EU and US Cross-Border Transfer mechanisms: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers outside EU/EEA, EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF) applicability, supplementary measures (encryption, localization), transfer to/from Singapore (GDPR adequacy / SCCs / APEC CBPR).
3. Recommended Server Architecture Strategy: Role of Singapore servers vs China servers for serving global users (EU, US, SEA) vs domestic mainland China users, avoiding unlawful outbound transfers of domestic China user data and ensuring compliant routing for EU/US users.
4. DPIA (GDPR) and PIPA (Personal Information Protection Assessment under PIPL Art 55) roadmap & checklist: Concrete step-by-step 6-month roadmap detailing phases, required legal/technical documentation, and audit milestones.
